text:
omar (People Ops): Quick Q 11 planning note: a teammate wants a flexible phased return after parental leave 12 weeks full, then 2 days/week for 6 weeks. Need to confirm payroll, benefits continuation, and what manager paperwork looks like. Any past experience?

nina (backend): We had someone do part-time after bonding. Key callouts: health benefits continue if you're on a paid leave schedule per payroll; if switching to <20h/week you might lose some coverage tiers. Manager filled out a Phased Return Agreement that listed hours per week and who covers oncall.

lucas (sre): Coverage wise: if they're oncall we usually reduce their rotation to 1 every 6 weeks for first month, and assign a shadow for alerts. Recommend notifying PagerDuty and updating rotation early.

omar (People Ops): Good, thanks. Do we need a separate form for intermittent days vs. a continuous phased block? Also timeline: what deadlines should we tell the employee to get docs in?

hr-bot: Forms & guidance: https://redwood-internal.example/hr/leave-portal. Required: Leave Request, Phased Return Agreement, and any medical certification if applicable. Submit 30 days before when possible; exceptions ok12contact people-ops@redwood.com for short notice.

zoe (payroll): Payroll note: Base parental pay covers continuous bonding up to 12 weeks. For intermittent/part-time weeks we calculate prorated pay for paid weeks and apply accrued PTO or unpaid leave rules for gaps. Send dates and weekly hours to payroll 10 business days prior to each pay period for accurate withholding.

nina (backend): Also log the arrangement in the employee's HR note and the team calendar so scheduling doesn't clash with sprint planning.

lucas (sre): Ops checklist I usually ask for: 1) primary services owned, 2) runbooks to update, 3) who covers alerts, 4) expected response SLAs during phased period.

omar (People Ops): I'll drop a one-page checklist and the Phased Return Agreement template into the shared drive and tag the manager. Who can volunteer to help draft the runbook updates?

nina (backend): I can help with runbook edits for services I touch.

zoe (payroll): And loop payroll in early for any pay proration so benefits deductions remain stable. If someone wants a benefit projection I can run a sample with dates + hours.

omar (People Ops): Great. I'll post the template link and a short FAQ for managers. If anyone wants to discuss a specific case, DM me or we can do a 15-min sync. Thanks all. :smile:
